leading_positions.synthesis: Six of the eight round-1 files prefer B005 (optical lattice clocks) as a single-part prize, all with the same two laureates, Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye. What is shared: the invention is a single idea (magic-wavelength trapping of many atoms) followed by a realization at about 1e-18, reproduced in several laboratories, with attribution that fits two names. What is not shared: the citation wording differs (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Danielsson mention magic-wavelength trapping, accuracy, or a new regime of precision, while Pearce's draft is the bare 'invention and realization of optical lattice clocks'), and the supporters do not agree on how firmly to separate the clock from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes or on whether other lattice-clock groups and ultrastable-laser developers weaken a two-name credit. Several supporters (Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Olsson, Pearce) name B014 as a first alternative or a serious competitor, and Danielsson, Johansson and Kroll note that their own first-choice rankings changed after reading the other opening ballots. Danielsson and Pearce, who opened on B055 and B035 respectively, now place B005 first or second and keep those entries only as alternatives.

Two files, Eriksson and Mehlig, prefer B014 (magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene) as a single-part prize with the same three names: Allan H. MacDonald, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero and Rafi Bistritzer, and nearly identical citation wording on flat bands at the magic angle plus correlated insulating and superconducting states. What is shared: a quantitative prediction (2011 continuum model) followed by a surprising 2018 experimental discovery, reproduced widely and opening moire quantum matter. What is not shared: Mehlig moved to this position from KPZ (B016) and had earlier treated Bistritzer as a junior name before accepting all three, while Eriksson ranks it first on the merits of the discovery. Both name B005 as a first alternative and both acknowledge that B014 leaves out Yuan Cao and earlier twisted-bilayer theorists, and that the superconducting mechanism is unsettled. Eriksson and Mehlig differ in how much weight to give maturity; Mehlig frames the choice as new-phenomenon prize versus measurement-science prize.

areas_of_agreement: All eight files propose a single-part prize built on either B005 or B014, and each file names the other of the two as an alternative (six B005 supporters list B014; Eriksson and Mehlig list B005). No file prefers any other ballot in its preferred configuration, including the entries ranked first in some opening ballots (B055, B035, B046, B016, B051), which appear only as alternatives or reservations.
For B005 every supporter proposes exactly Katori and Ye, and nobody argues for a different or larger named set in a preferred configuration.

For B014 both supporters propose MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer, and all eight files accept that the pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved while treating the discovery of correlated states as stable and widely reproduced.

Members generally agree that the B005 citation should be kept narrow, tied to the lattice clock invention and not to precision timekeeping or ultrastable lasers in general, and that the B014 citation should stay with flat bands and observed correlated phases and not with an explanation of superconductivity.
Members agree that the practical payoff of B005 (redefinition of the second) is an application not yet realized, though they disagree on whether that matters for timing.
scientific_disputes: Whether the lattice clock is a discovery-grade conceptual step or primarily a precision-measurement and instrumentation advance: Danielsson and Mehlig raise this, and Mehlig asks whether a clock is a new discovery about nature, as moire quantum matter is, or an instrument achievement; B005 supporters (Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Johansson) argue that magic-wavelength trapping is a separate conceptual step that changes the statistical and systematic budget.

How far B005 overlaps the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 prize for control of single quantum systems (including ion clocks): supporters treat those prizes as enabling context, while Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce each record the overlap as a reservation.

Whether the unsettled pairing mechanism and sample-level questions in twisted bilayer graphene (strain, disorder, variability) reduce the weight of the 2018 discovery, or whether the discovery of correlated states is stable irrespective of mechanism (Eriksson and Mehlig argue the latter; Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Olsson and Pearce press the former).

Whether the 2011 continuum model supplied the first quantitative magic-angle flat-band condition relative to the earlier twisted-bilayer band-structure results of Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto; Eriksson and Mehlig note this rests on recollection and has not been verified from the supplied material.
attribution_disputes: B005: other strontium and ytterbium lattice-clock groups (named variously as Paris, PTB and others) and ultrastable-laser developers are outside the credited pair; Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson record this, Kroll and Johansson say fine priority between the Tokyo and Boulder efforts is from memory and should be checked, and Danielsson asks whether Ye's contribution is co-invention or record-accuracy realization.

B014: Yuan Cao, lead author of the 2018 experiments, and other experimental groups such as Cory Dean's are not credited, and earlier twisted-bilayer theorists (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) are outside the trio; Eriksson argues that a prize normally credits the group leader, while others find the three-seat limit forces an arguable cut.

B014: whether Bistritzer belongs beside MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero; Mehlig initially treated him as a junior third name, then accepted the three-name list, while Johansson (not a B014 supporter) says he would credit the pair or the trio only if the 2011 model is judged a joint result, and Olsson and Eriksson argue the 2011 paper is a joint result.

Alternatives that were raised but not preferred show similar credit problems: B055 (five credited names for three seats), B035 (IceCube names versus DUMAND, Baikal and AMANDA pioneers), B046 (Wallraff not credited), B016 (Parisi, an original KPZ author, not credited), and B024 and B015 (how to treat Zoller across the two ballots).
maturity_disputes: B014 dates from 2018 experiments, about eight years; Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Olsson and Pearce regard that as a shorter record than two decades for B005, while Eriksson and Mehlig note unusually fast reproduction by many groups and Eriksson sees no reason the case will improve by waiting.

B005: whether the pending redefinition of the second should be treated as a maturity concern (Eriksson's opening reservation; Pearce, Mehlig and Olsson note the payoff is prospective) or as a pending application that does not affect validity (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth).
Whether the committee should weigh a field that is moving quickly now (Eriksson) against a settled topic whose interpretation has been stable (the B005 supporters).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson-goran directs WACQT and works in superconducting circuits and quantum computing, so B046 (and less directly B024 and B015) are close to the member's own field; the file states the member should not press B046 and would consider recusal on it. None of these is a preferred configuration in round 1.

Olsson-eva's opening first choice B051 is close to her own field of transmission electron microscopy; she did not place it first in round 1 and would step back from deciding on it. B051 is only an alternative in her file.

Eriksson-olle flags field proximity (electronic-structure theory of two-dimensional materials) to B014 as proximity and not a documented tie, and invites colleagues to test his judgment; no personal or institutional tie to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer is documented.
Mehlig-bernhard flags that B016 (KPZ, non-equilibrium statistical physics) is close to his research area and says he demoted it for that reason; no conflict is apparent for B014 or B005.

Kroll-stefan discloses a doctoral-period research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder; Hall is not a candidate, but the precision-laser community is adjacent to B005. He also notes that Zoller's quantum-memory and quantum-optics community overlaps with his field if B024 or B015 were pursued.
Lindroth-eva flags that she is a theoretical atomic physicist in an adjacent area to B005 and may overweight a precision-atomic argument; no specific conflict is documented.

Pearce-mark (chair) notes field proximity to astroparticle candidates such as B035 (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGO+ and XL-Calibur collaborations), with no documented IceCube tie; B035 is only an alternative in the chair's file.
Danielsson-ulf notes two years at CERN after the PhD as a general institutional link to B055, with no recorded tie to any of its named individuals; B055 is only an alternative in his file.
questions_for_round2: B005 versus B014 as the single lead: does the committee value a mature, tightly attributed measurement-science invention (B005) or a younger new-phenomenon discovery with an unsettled mechanism (B014), and what explicit criterion should decide this between them?

For B005, can the three-seat limit and a two-name credit survive scrutiny of the Tokyo, Boulder, Paris and PTB lattice-clock priority record and of ultrastable-laser contributions, and who first published the magic-wavelength proposal and the first lattice spectroscopy?

For B005, does the committee consider the lattice clock sufficiently distinct from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize, and what exact citation wording (magic-wavelength lattice, accuracy near 1e-18, or both) would keep the claim to the invention and realization?
Is Ye's contribution best worded as co-invention or as realization at record accuracy, and should the citation say so?

For B014, is the three-name list (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer) defensible given the omission of Yuan Cao and earlier twisted-bilayer theorists, or would a two-name or differently composed list be fairer, and what would a citation limited to flat bands and observed correlated states say?

Does the approximately eight-year record of B014 and the unresolved superconducting mechanism count as insufficient maturity, and does the pending redefinition of the second count against B005 or only as an unrealized application?

Should any ballot raised only as an alternative (B035, B055, B046, B016, B024, B015, B051) be advanced given the attribution problems each member identified, or does round 2 confine itself to B005 and B014?

Which members, if any, should step back on specific ballots (Johansson on B046, Olsson on B051, Mehlig on B016), and does field proximity for Eriksson on B014 or Lindroth and Kroll on B005 warrant any change in how their statements are weighed?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows two stated positions rather than a consensus: six explicit supporters of a single-part B005 prize (Katori and Ye) and two of a single-part B014 prize (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer), with each side naming the other as its first alternative. Both cases rest on a clear conceptual step and broad independent reproduction; the main differences are the length of the track record, the nature of the claim (instrument achievement versus new phenomenon), and the completeness of the credit list. Both leading positions have attribution gaps that members agree cannot be settled from the supplied credited names alone, and the committee has not yet tested these points against sources.
